description:
FILED s446k (Opus, agent K of round 5), found by the #463 items 3-5 probes.
PRE-EXISTING: the symbolic spelling `*{"!"}` has always taken this path; s446k
only routed the `*!` spelling onto it.

  no strict 'refs';
  $! = 2;
  print "a=[$!]\n";                 perl: No such file or directory   PCL: same
  our $Y; *Y = *{"!"};
  print "b=[$Y]\n";                 perl: No such file or directory   PCL: []
  our $Z; *Z = *!;
  print "c=[$Z]\n";                 perl: No such file or directory   PCL: []

So PCL's `$!` works, but it is not backed by an ordinary glob slot the alias
can reach: the alias installs nothing and reads "".  `%-` DOES alias correctly
(`*X = *-` then `$X{foo}` -- probed, s446k), so this is specific to the magic
variables PCL COMPUTES rather than stores.

SECOND HALF, worse: `%!` (the errno hash) is not implemented at all --

  print 0 < keys(%!) ? "has" : "empty";
    perl: has
    PCL:  "The variable %! is unbound" at LOAD -- the whole file dies

t/re/reg_namedcapture.t is exactly this file: `*Y = *!;` then
`0 < keys(%Y)`.  After s446k it produces two honest `not ok` rows (0 ok / 2
notok, up from an abort at the drop); with %! and the alias it would pass.

SHAPE: the question is where the magic scalars/hashes live in the box model
and whether `p-glob-assign`/`p-make-typeglob` can name their slots.  Decide
that before writing anything -- a per-name special case in the glob path is
the wrong layer.  Read `docs/ir-spec.md` Â§magic globals first.


RULED s449 (Fable, 2026-08-29): DESIGN COMPLETE -- docs/computed-magic-design-s449.md.  Scalar half: canonical MAGIC BOXES (|$!|, |$^E|) defvar-d beside |$.| (the live precedent), getter/setter = p-errno-string and its setf -- the accessor IS the getter (rule 11); emission UNCHANGED; ZERO glob-path changes (p-glob-copy already shares slot boxes; the bug was only that |$!| was unbound).  %! half: a REAL hash-table on |%!| whose VALUES are p-magic-cell boxes over a new *p-errno-table* (fixed POSIX name list resolved via sb-posix at boot); %p-hash-unbox-elem gains the magic-cell arm p-aref-unbox-elem already has (one arm); NOT an %ENV-style marker.  #602 folds into the same session (clear-then-copy shape (a)).  Follow-on separate task: lib/Errno.pm shim over the same table (rule 9a).  Bar in the doc SS6.  Scheduled: Opus round 8, cl/-only, no gen bump.

DONE s450t (Opus, round 8 agent T), commit "s450t (Opus): #561 â a COMPUTED
magic gets a CANONICAL BOX...".  Shipped exactly as designed
(docs/computed-magic-design-s449.md SS3-4), with ONE thing the design did not
foresee.

WHAT LANDED
  * |$!| and |$^E| are defvar'd boxes holding a p-magic-cell whose getter and
    setter ARE p-errno-string / (setf p-errno-string).  ZERO glob-path changes
    were needed, exactly as ruled: `*Y = *!`, `*Z = *{"!"}`, `\$Y` through the
    alias, a WRITE through the alias reaching C errno, and `local $!` are all
    byte-identical to perl 5.40.3.  The %SPECIAL_VARS audit found exactly the
    two accessor-emitted entries the design named; the ['p-undef'] stubs were
    left alone.
  * |%!| is a real hash table of 134 magic values.  Numbers come from sb-posix
    where it exposes the constant; the eleven glibc names it does NOT export
    (ECANCELED EHWPOISON EISNAM EKEYEXPIRED EKEYREJECTED EKEYREVOKED ENOKEY
    ENOTRECOVERABLE ENOTSUP EOWNERDEAD ERFKILL) carry the number in
    *p-errno-name-numbers*, on the *p-signal-numbers* precedent, so that
    `keys %!` is perl's key set and not sb-posix's subset.  MEASURED: the 123
    sb-posix does export agree with perl's Errno to the number.
  * PROBED BEFORE WRITING THE GETTER, and the obvious guess was wrong in both
    halves: $!{NAME} is the errno NUMBER when $! holds that errno and 0
    otherwise -- never 1, and ALWAYS DEFINED.  A STORE is fatal in perl
    ("ERRNO hash is read only!"), so the setter dies.
  * %p-hash-unbox-elem gained the magic-cell arm; p-values / p-each /
    p-gethash were verified to funnel through it (no second dispatch).

THE DEVIATION, and it was necessary: `$!{ENOENT}` was NOT reading %!.  The
element-access container is built by swapping the sigil in the RENDERED
scalar, and $! renders as (p-errno-string) -- a FORM no sigil swap reaches --
so `$!{ENOENT}` emitted (p-gethash (p-errno-string) "ENOENT"), a symbolic hash
named by the strerror text, answering undef SILENTLY.
Pl::ExprToCL::_bare_container_sym re-renders from the aggregate spelling for
the four %SPECIAL_VARS names that render as a compound form, and only those.
Generation v2-355 -> v2-365, three artifacts regenerated (bodies identical).
Blast radius measured: corpus-diff IDENTICAL over 111; emission A/B over lib/
+ perl's own t/ (605) + shapes = 1 real diff in 634, t/op/require_errors.t's
own `$!{ENOENT}`.

MOVER: t/re/reg_namedcapture.t 0 ok / 2 notok -> 1 ok / 1 notok (run alone).
It does NOT reach 2/0: test 1 is `eval '*X{HASH}{X} || 1'`, and a subscript on
a glob-slot access is a compiler DROP (task #671); even un-dropped it needs
task #672 (%- values must be ARRAYREFS, not the capture string).

GUARD: Pl/t/errno-magic-01.t (8 rows, each against the live perl answer).
DOCS: ir-spec SS8 gains the canonical-box rule, %! in the table, and the
swap-before-the-magic-table rule; not-supported.md's English.pm section and
Pl/t/english-01.t's header were STALE ("$! is a call into C errno, not a
variable at all") and were repaired in the same commit.
FILED: #670 (%! residue), #671, #672, #673 (lib/Errno.pm shim -- the design's
named follow-on, NOT built here), #674 (English.pm may drop the errno ties).

DO NOT RETRY: an %ENV-style marker for %! (rejected by the design and by the
chokepoint count); a per-name special case anywhere in the glob path (the slot
just had to exist).
subject: A glob alias to a MAGIC punctuation variable yields an empty slot -- `*Y = *!` then `$Y` reads "" where perl gives the errno string; and `%!` is not implemented at all (unbound CL variable, whole file dead)
